newsitem.title: USA: Illinois governor praises Moody's upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Illinois governor praises Moody's upgrade.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar said Monday that upgrades of the state's general obligation and Build Illinois sales tax revenue bond ratings to Aa3 from A1 by Moody's Investors Service "underscores that the state's fiscal house is back in order."

"Our fiscal discipline obviously has paid off. We have fully escaped the fiscal quicksand that I found when I became governor six years ago," Edgar said in a news release. "The state of Illinois now stands on firm fiscal ground. And we have done it by controlling spending rather than by raising general taxes."
Moody's cited Illinois's improved financial condition for the upgrades, which affect $5.3 billion of outstanding GO debt and $1.6 billion of Build Illinois debt.

However, the statement released by Edgar's press office did not address a warning issued by Moody's over state appropriations for $19.2 million of insured, 1996 certificate of participation issue that is being challenged in court by a group of Democratic state lawmakers.
Moody's warned in its credit release that failure to appropriate for COPs debt could have negative rating repercussions for the state's GO and appropriation-derived debt.

Moody's comments on the COPs came in the wake of comments last month by State Rep. Jeff Schoenberg, D-Evanston, one of the plaintiffs in the lawsuit, and new chairman of the House Appropriations Committee.

Schoenberg said that House Democrats may not be willing to appropriate funds for debt service on the COPs, which were sold last year as part of a lease-purchase agreement entered into by the Illinois Department of Central Management Services for a new public aid building in downtown Chicago.
On Monday, Schoenberg said Moody's comments underscore the seriousness of resolving the COPs issue," as well as the Democratic lawmakers' position that the COPs are "indeed state indebtedness."
He said legislation will be introduced this session to reform "the current lack of accountability in issuing COPs."
